memberdef.name: runChildProcess

briefdescription.para: Child-process setup: connect stdio to the PTY slave and exec the shell.

detaileddescription.para: Called in the child after fork(). Never returns on success; calls _exit(1) on execlp failure.

listitem.para: Close the master fd (child does not need it).
Change to the specified working directory (if provided).
setsid() — create a new session so the child becomes a session leader.
ioctl(TIOCSCTTY) — make the slave the controlling terminal of the session.
Close the slave fd if it is not already one of the standard fds.
Set TERM=xterm-256color so the shell and TUI apps use 256-colour sequences.
Set LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 if not already set, so child shell uses UTF-8 character classification (works around inherited invalid LANG=UTF-8 on macOS).
execvp(shell, argv) — replace the process image with the shell. Short names (e.g. "zsh") are resolved via $PATH.

parameterdescription.para: Master fd to close in the child.
Slave fd to use as the controlling terminal and stdio.
Shell program name or absolute path (C string, must outlive fork).
Optional working directory to chdir to before exec.
Additional environment variable pairs to export in the child.

simplesect.para: Runs in the child process only. Must not return.

briefdescription.para: macOS / Linux PTY implementation: openpty, fork, read/write, resize, shutdown.

detaileddescription.para: All PTY interaction goes through the master file descriptor. The master is set to O_NONBLOCK after fork so the reader thread can drain it without blocking. poll() is used to wait for data with a timeout, keeping the reader thread responsive to resize requests and thread-exit signals.
